purpose: Test append-and-replay handling for late events, monotone watermarks and causal parent arrival.

activities.label: process a finite stream with monotone watermarks and late events
compare online snapshots and batch replay across permutations
attack late-event retention, monotone watermarks and causal authority

queries.expression: are late events retained and replayed instead of silently dropped
does final batch replay converge across event permutations
does missing causal authority remain UNKNOWN while late parents can resolve pending claims

assumptions: A watermark is an operational lower bound on expected future event time, not an eternal proof of completeness.
A late event may revise a previously settled projection and must remain in the append-only ledger.
Source version and explicit parent IDs provide the minimum causal contract for this finite fixture.
A source correction may supersede a previous event without deleting its history.
This experiment is local and synthetic, so no network or human data is needed.
kill_tests: Dropping a late correction blocks the expected projection.
A drop-late policy blocks the contract.
A conflicting duplicate delivery blocks ingestion.
A correction without supersession history blocks.
Missing causal authority cannot become a supported fact.
A causal child detached from its parent blocks.
unknowns: How watermarks should be coordinated across partitions and independent sources.
Whether source versions or vector clocks are necessary for each production adapter.
How to make late-event replay atomic with an external action.
How to sign, authenticate and rotate event deliveries.
How much provisional state can be shown to a human without causing wrong action.
